newsitem.title: USA: WHX raises Dynamics bid to $172 million.
newsitem.headline: WHX raises Dynamics bid to $172 million.

text.p: WHX Corp., parent of Wheeling-Pittsburgh Steel Corp., said Wednesday it raised its unsolicited takeover bid for Dynamics Corp. of America to $172 million from $152 million.
Dynamics, a diversified electronic components maker, had rejected the earlier bid as being "totally inadequate," and said Wednesday it would respond to the new bid by Monday.
WHX raised its bid to $45 a share from $40 a share for all of Dynamics's outstanding 3.82 million shares.

WHX has proposed to take over Dynamics by buying 19.9 percent of its outstanding shares, which would give it enough leverage to elect a slate of directors that would make a takeover possible, without setting off a poison pill takeover defence.
WHX said it was willing to negotiate a friendly merger "and thereby avoid the necessity of a proxy contest for corporate control."

It said, however, that as it previously announced, it plans to solicit proxies for Dynamics' annual meeting, scheduled for May 2, to elect four of its nominees to Dynamics's board and amend by-laws of the company.
Dynamics stock closed at $44, up $3.875, and WHX closed at $6.875, unchanged, both on the New York Stock Exchange.
The latest bid may have a better chance of succeeding. Mario Gabelli, whose Gabelli Funds owns about 20 percent of Dynamics' outstanding shares, said he would consider the bid.
"Essentially, (WHX Chairman) Ron Labow has crafted a compelling bid for shareholders of Dynamics and clearly we're examining the bid," Gabelli said.
